question: King Porus and Alexander the Great fought which battle?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Battle of Hydaspes__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​​​​​​​​​**

__
 
• Porus

 
 
• **Porus was an Indian prince** who governed the area between the** Hydaspes (Jhelum) and Acesines (Chenab) rivers** during the conquest of the Punjab by Alexander the Great (327–326 bce).** **
 
• **Porus resisted Alexander,** in contrast to his neighbour, Ambhi, king of Taxila (Takshashila).
 
• In his capacity as** King of Macedonia and Persia **and one of history's greatest military strategists, Alexander the Great built the biggest **empire the ancient world had ever known**.
 
• **Alexander the Great and King Porus **engaged in combat in the** Hydaspes in 326 BC**.
 
• It occurred along the Jhelum River's banks in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent, which the Greeks called** Hydaspes (modern-day Punjab, Pakistan).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​​​**​​​Battle of Hydaspes

 
 
• **Battle of Hydaspes **is significant because it was during this conflict in India along the banks of the **Hydaspes River **that Alexander the Great came the closest to losing.
 
• The fearless** King Porus resisted being completely subdued** by his dreaded Companion cavalry.
 
• **Alexander's career of conquest came to an end **with the defeat of Hydaspes; he passed away before beginning a new offensive.
 
• **Yogi Adityanath**, the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, said that Chandragupta Maurya, who established the Mauryan empire in the fourth century BC, had won a war against **Alexander of Macedon, **yet historians have chosen to refer to Alexander as the "great" one. 
 
• **Alexander was drawn to India because of its richness. **
 
• In addition, he was said to have a significant interest in natural history and geographic research.
 
• Before Alexander's invasion, there were numerous petty kings in northwest India,** including Ambhi of Taxila and Porus of the Jhelum region (Hydaspes). **
